text: 🇲🇽🛢️ Pemex was the neoliberals' "petty cash." "They said they had responsible finances because their deficit was tiny. But who did they pile the debt onto? Pemex — with no results, just to prop up public spending. That's the truth." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Under Peña Nieto, Pemex debt climbed from $64 billion to $113 billion. This government cut it by $20 billion and says Pemex needs almost no federal support in 2027.

🇲🇽✊ "Where did they cut? In health, in education." "In the neoliberal era, health and education were exactly where they cut. The so-called 'austerity' never touched top officials' salaries or the money handed to the media." — President Claudia Sheinbaum She set that record against the 2027 budget: education +10.7%, science +13%, health +11.3%. The gap between the richest and poorest tenth fell from 34x in 2008 to 16x in 2024.

🇲🇽🌎 Sheinbaum draws the red line in the USMCA talks. "Let the people of Mexico know: we will not sign anything that harms our sovereignty or our economy. What we're seeking are better trade terms." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the U.S. trade negotiations Mexico is pressing Washington to cut steel, aluminum and auto tariffs and add no new ones, while refusing to trade away sovereignty on the 54 "non-tariff barriers" on the table.

🚨🇲🇽 Media silence on the arrest of Cerimedo, the operator who targeted Sheinbaum. "Not a single outlet covered the arrest of Cerimedo, a partner in La Derecha Diario — who, by their own admission, set out to attack the President of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum At least five Latin American presidents have moved to distance themselves from the network. Sheinbaum says foreign electoral manipulation — and AI-driven disinformation — must be regulated.

🇲🇽⚖️ "The VAT is a very regressive tax" — Sheinbaum rejects raising it. "The VAT hits those who have the least the hardest. We do not agree with raising the VAT rate." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Since 2019 revenue has risen 2.7 trillion pesos with no tax hike — only by fighting evasion — versus 1.5 trillion under Peña Nieto's fiscal reform and gas hikes.

🔥🇲🇽 1.6 trillion pesos paid on Fobaproa — and the debt only grew. "We have paid nearly 1.6 trillion pesos over the years, and not a single peso of the principal has been paid off — on the contrary, it has grown." — Finance Secretary Édgar Amador, at the mañanera The bank bailout was locked in by a PAN and PRI vote in December 1998. For 2027 the budget still sets aside about 48 billion pesos for it — and bank IPAB fees will no longer be tax-deductible.

🇲🇽✊ No new taxes, no gas hikes: Mexico's 2027 budget. "There are no new taxes, and there will be no gas price hikes. We are not putting the country into debt, as some like to claim." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The package lifts tax revenue 5.9% in real terms by cracking down on shell-company invoicing and evasion — not by taxing people — while cutting the deficit from 4.1% to 3.9% of GDP.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's trade surplus is up nearly 7× in 2026</u>

Mexico's trade surplus hit 9,857 million dollars in the first half of 2026 — almost seven times the 1,433 million registered a year earlier, per INEGI figures reported by El Economista. In July alone total exports reached 81.42 billion dollars, a 43.7% annual jump, with manufacturing up 45.7% and electrical and electronic goods soaring 134%. That's the export engine of a country Washington keeps threatening with tariffs, breaking its own records anyway.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico City puts 8,176 cops on the street — and 20,000 residents watching them</u>

Mayor Clara Brugada launched "Código 1: Police on Your Street," deploying 8,176 officers across two shifts with 2,044 new patrol vehicles and GPS tracking on every route. The twist is accountability from below: more than 20,000 citizen volunteers — scaling toward 60,000 — will document whether police actually show up. "We're transforming proximity patrols through three pillars: territorial evidence, technological evidence, and citizen evaluation," Brugada said. It comes as CDMX logs its lowest homicide count in 29 years.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The PRI's "opposition" leader: 800M pesos a year and homes in Texas</u>

Alejandro "Alito" Moreno — the PRI boss who calls Mexico's government authoritarian — pulls in roughly 800 million pesos a year in public money through the INE to run his party. Contralínea lays out the rest: 83.5 million pesos allegedly embezzled during his Campeche governorship (2015-2019), 36 million more diverted through shell-company invoices, and properties stacked across Houston, Spring and Katy, Texas. Five separate FGR investigations are open. This is the same man caught on tape in 2022 saying journalists "shouldn't be shot — they should be starved."
